newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks slip on profit-taking.

text.p: Mild profit-taking halted the bull run on most European stock markets on Thursday but dealers forecast that buyers would soon be back.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar dipped due to comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on its recent surge against the mark but later recovered.

In stocks, most markets got off to a storming start but soon fell back as investors cashed in on this week's strong gains. However, floor trading in Frankurt closed at a record high, as did the Milan and Vienna markets.

London typified the trend on most of the leading European bourses. Soon after the opening the FTSE-100 index of blue chips came within seven points of the psychological 5,000-point barrier but then the selling began.
"It's a natural correction," said one London dealer. "The market needed to catch its breath but it will have another go at 5,000."
The FTSE closed down 15.2 points at 4,949.0 after Wall Street also opened lower on profit-taking following the Dow's break through 8,000 points on Wednesday.
But some London traders forecast that the buyers would soon be back even if this defies economic logic as British interest rates rise and a strong pound punishes exporters.
"There has been no real change in sentiment," said Ian Williams, UK equity strategist at Panmure Gordon. "People were just taking a few profits and waiting for the next leg upwards."
Profit-takers targeted pharmaceutical stocks but other sectors fared better. "Pharmaceuticals got slaughtered today yet we were only down 15 points, which is quite encouraging really," said Williams.

In Germany, the DAX index closed up 26.07 points at a record 4,227.31. But this did not give the full picture as the DAX measures only floor trade which closes at 1200 GMT. Prices fell in later German electronic trade and the IBIS index, which measures it, closed down 19.78 points or 0.47 percent at 4,203.91.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index of blue chips stormed through 3,000 points at the opening for the first time but after its own bout of profit-taking closed down 29.42 points or 0.98 percent at 2,958.59.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar drifted gently lower but traders saw it gathering strength for the next move up as it consolidated this week's strong gains.
The dollar slipped after Bundesbank chief Tietmeyer said he hoped the correction of the mark against the dollar would not go too far.

"For the most part exchange rate developments are the result of corrections which were necessary. I hope now that it will not come to an overreaction," he said. "We are watching developments very carefully."

The dollar also stumbled after senior Finance Ministry official Hansgeorg Hauser said Germany would insist on a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty when it came to choosing which countries would qualify for European monetary union.
A belief that monetary union would begin with a broad swathe of members, breeding a euro which is weaker than the mark, has been a major factor in the German unit's decline.

But the dollar later recovered due to market perceptions that Germany is not too worried about the mark weakness which helps its exporters. "The Germans don't mind a weak mark. It's the only thing that's going to drag their economy back up," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in London.
At the European close the dollar stood at 1.7898 marks, down from an early high of 1.8020 and late Wednesday's 1.7980. It was easier at 116.07 yen compared with 116.27 late Wednesday in Europe.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 116.07 yen and 1.7898 marks compared with 116.27 yen and 1.7980 marks in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed 15.2 lower at 4,949.0.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade closed up 26.07 points or 0.62 percent at a record 4,227.31. In later electronic trade the IBIS index closed down 19.78 points or 0.47 percent at 4,203.91.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 29.42 points or 0.98 percent at 2,958.59.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed up 10 cents at $319.55 an ounce. Silver was down nine cents at $4.21.
